title: TotalEnergies Buys Back €38 Million of Its Own Shares Over Two Days
text: TotalEnergies SE repurchased 590,596 of its own shares for approximately €38 million on the Paris market on February 12 and 13, 2026. This buyback is part of the company's capital management strategy, aiming to enhance shareholder value and demonstrate confidence in its financial position. It aligns with a broader trend among energy companies returning cash to shareholders amidst strong cash flows.

title: TotalEnergies SE: Disclosure of Transactions in Own Shares
text: TotalEnergies SE disclosed transactions in its own shares from February 12 to February 13, 2026, totaling 590,596 shares. The company repurchased these shares at an average price of 64.341617 EUR per share, amounting to approximately 38 million EUR. This disclosure is in accordance with authorizations from the shareholders’ general meeting on May 23, 2025.

title: TotalEnergies (TTE) Expands EV Charging Network in Belgium and Netherlands
text: TotalEnergies (TTE) has announced a partnership with Tikehau Capital to develop electric vehicle charging stations in Belgium and the Netherlands, focusing on public spaces. This collaboration aims to assist local authorities in their EV transition and strengthen TotalEnergies' presence in the Benelux region. Additionally, TotalEnergies recently secured a 10-year contract to supply 800 gigawatt-hours of renewable energy to paper maker SWM's facilities in France.

title: TotalEnergies Marketing India Hosts Annual Distributor Convention to Unveil Future Growth Strategy
text: TotalEnergies Marketing India Private Limited (TEMIPL) held its annual lubricants distributor convention in Hyderabad, India, gathering 200 distributors and partners. The company unveiled its 2026 strategic roadmap, focusing on strengthening its distribution network, launching new products, and recognizing distributor excellence. This strategy aims to drive sustainable growth and innovation in the Indian automotive aftermarket, emphasizing the crucial role of distributors in the company's success.

title: TotalEnergies (TTE) Expands EV Charging Network in Belgium and Netherlands
text: TotalEnergies SE (TTE) has recently expanded its electric vehicle charging network in Belgium and the Netherlands through a partnership with Tikehau Capital. This collaboration aims to develop charging infrastructure in public places across both countries, supporting the local transition to electric vehicles and strengthening TotalEnergies' presence in the Benelux region. Additionally, TotalEnergies announced a 10-year agreement to supply 800 gigawatt-hours of renewable energy to paper maker SWM's French facilities.

title: TotalEnergies: LNG Exposure And AI Power Demand Offer Structural Growth
text: TotalEnergies (TTE) is rated as a "Buy" due to strong financials, robust free cash flow, and a significant cost-saving plan, offering a solid dividend yield and projected total shareholder yield above 7% in 2026. title: TotalEnergies Expects Mexico’s Energía Costa Azul LNG Terminal to Enter Service This Year
text: TotalEnergies SE anticipates that new LNG export projects, including the Energía Costa Azul terminal in Mexico and facilities in Qatar, will begin operations this year. These projects are expected to counteract a decline in global natural gas prices by increasing supply. The company is actively expanding its LNG portfolio and foresees a rise in its oil and gas production.

title: TotalEnergies SE: Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2025 Results
text: TotalEnergies SE reported strong financial results for the fourth quarter and full year 2025, with stable cash flow despite a drop in oil prices. The company's adjusted net income for 2025 was $15.6 billion, and cash flow reached $27.8 billion, benefiting from production growth and strategic investments in low-carbon energies. TotalEnergies announced a 5.6% increase in its 2025 dividend to €3.40 per share and outlined plans for continued profitable transition, including a 5% increase in overall energy production for 2026.

title: Indicative dates for 2026 dividends
text: TotalEnergies has announced the indicative payment dates for its 2026 interim and final dividends, following a Board of Directors meeting on February 10, 2026. These dates apply to shares listed on the NYSE, with separate ex-dividend and payment dates for Euronext. The company cautions that future dividend payments are subject to board and shareholder approval and other factors.

title: TotalEnergies Q4 includes USD 700m offshore wind impairment
text: TotalEnergies announced a USD 700 million impairment related to its offshore wind assets in its Q4 results. This financial adjustment highlights challenges within the offshore wind sector. The article also lists other recent news in renewables, including new wind projects and financial updates from other companies.

title: TotalEnergies Cuts Buyback to Lower End of Range
text: TotalEnergies SE has reduced its share buybacks to $750 million for the first quarter, the lower end of its guided range, to manage debt amid lower oil prices. The company's adjusted net income fell by 13% in the fourth quarter, aligning with analyst estimates. Despite the cut, TotalEnergies aims to maintain a healthy balance sheet, with CEO Patrick Pouyanne stating intentions to balance cash generation with expenditure in an uncertain environment.

title: TotalEnergies proposes a dividend of 3.40€/share for fiscal year 2025, a 5.6% increase
text: TotalEnergies' Board of Directors has proposed a dividend of 3.40 €/share for fiscal year 2025, representing a 5.6% increase from the previous year. This proposal will be put to a Shareholders’ Meeting on May 29, 2026, with the final dividend of 0.85 €/share expected to be detached and paid in cash according to a schedule in July 2026. The company also provided details on the payment timeline and exchange rate information for NYSE-listed shares.

title: Oil giant TotalEnergies on Trump's Venezuela dream: ‘Too expensive and too polluting'
text: TotalEnergies has stated it is "too expensive and too polluting" to return to Venezuela, despite U.S. President Donald Trump's urging for oil majors to invest in the country. The French energy company exited Venezuela in 2022 due to its strategy shift from heavy crude and safety concerns. Other companies, like Exxon Mobil, have also expressed caution regarding investments in the Venezuelan market.

title: United States: TotalEnergies to Provide 1 GW of Solar Capacity to Power Google’s Data Centers in Texas for 15 Years
text: TotalEnergies has signed two long-term Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) to supply 1 GW of solar capacity, equivalent to 28 TWh of renewable electricity over 15 years, to Google's data centers in Texas. This power will come from TotalEnergies-owned Wichita and Mustang Creek solar sites, with construction beginning in Q2 2026. This significant agreement marks TotalEnergies' largest renewable PPA in the US and aligns with its strategy to provide tailored renewable energy solutions for decarbonization goals, particularly for data centers.

title: TotalEnergies takes full ownership of Zeeland refinery from co-owner Lukoil - Reuters (TTE:NYSE)
text: TotalEnergies has acquired the remaining 45% stake in the Zeeland refinery in the Netherlands from Lukoil, giving it 100% ownership. The 180,000 bbl/day refinery is now fully controlled by TotalEnergies, though details on the payment for the shares were not immediately clear.

title: Exclusive: TotalEnergies takes over Zeeland refinery operations, Lukoil still owns 45%
text: TotalEnergies has taken over full operational control of the Zeeland refinery in the Netherlands, according to CEO Patrick Pouyanne. While TotalEnergies now manages all operations, including crude supply and output, Russia's Lukoil retains its 45% stake in the refinery and is actively seeking a buyer for its share. This arrangement is temporary and was prompted by U.S. sanctions on Lukoil and the ongoing situation regarding its international assets.

title: TotalEnergies SE: Information Concerning the Total Number of Voting Rights and Shares in the Share Capital as at January 31, 2026
text: TotalEnergies SE has released information regarding its total number of voting rights and shares as of January 31, 2026. The company reported 2,206,585,543 total shares, with an equal number of theoretical voting rights, and 2,142,085,069 exercisable voting rights after accounting for treasury shares. This notice is in accordance with French commercial and AMF regulations.

title: Workers at TotalEnergies' La Mede refinery seek redress for benzene exposure, union says
text: More than 180 workers and subcontractors at TotalEnergies' La Mede refinery will file complaints in a French labour court seeking compensation for benzene exposure. The CGT union stated that the complaints will address anxiety-related harm, with the potential for further claims if illnesses develop. Energy companies are increasingly facing similar lawsuits due to the health risks associated with chemical exposure.

title: TotalEnergies to Report Q4 Earnings: What to Expect This Season?
text: TotalEnergies (TTE) is scheduled to report its Q4 2025 earnings on February 11. The company expects a 4% year-over-year improvement in hydrocarbon production, driven by the restart of Ichthys LNG. While the Zacks Consensus Estimate predicts a decline in both earnings and revenues compared to the previous year, factors like strong hydrocarbon production, strategic acquisitions, and a focus on renewable energy are expected to influence the results.

title: TotalEnergies Strikes 1 GW Solar Deal to Power Google Data Centers in Texas
text: TotalEnergies has signed two long-term power purchase agreements with Google to supply 1 GW of solar capacity for Google’s data centers in Texas for 15 years. The electricity will be sourced from the new Wichita and Mustang Creek solar projects, which are scheduled to begin construction in Q2 2026. This agreement marks TotalEnergies' largest U.S. renewable PPA and strengthens its role in providing clean power to major digital customers while supporting the grid and creating jobs in Texas.

title: United States: TotalEnergies to Provide 1 GW of Solar Capacity to Power Google’s Data Centers in Texas for 15 Years

title: Namibia Government Says It Wasn’t Notified of PEL 104 Stake Sale
text: Namibia's energy ministry was not notified of TotalEnergies SE's and Petroleo Brasileiro SA's planned acquisition of stakes in the offshore exploration license PEL 104. TotalEnergies will buy a 42.5% operated stake from Eight Offshore Investments Holdings and Maravilla Oil & Gas, while Brazil’s Petrobras acquired another 42.5% stake. The state-owned Namcor will retain a 10% stake, and Eight Offshore Investments will hold the remaining 5%.

text: Jefferies analyst Mark Wilson maintained a Buy rating on TotalEnergies SE (TTE) with an average price target of $72.90, implying a 16.52% upside. title: Namibia: TotalEnergies Expands its Exploration Portfolio as Operator of PEL104 License
text: TotalEnergies has signed agreements to acquire a 42.5% operated interest in the PEL104 Exploration license in offshore Namibia, located in the Lüderitz basin and covering approximately 11,000 km². This move strengthens TotalEnergies' position in Namibia, following a previous acquisition in December, as the company progresses with the development of Venus and Mopane discoveries while continuing to explore prolific resources to benefit the country and its stakeholders. The transaction is subject to regulatory and joint venture approvals.

title: Namibia: TotalEnergies Expands its Exploration Portfolio as Operator of PEL104 License
text: TotalEnergies has signed agreements to acquire a 42.5% operated interest in the PEL104 Exploration license offshore Namibia, increasing its presence in the region. title: TotalEnergies expands its exploration portfolio offshore Namibia
text: TotalEnergies has acquired a 42.5% operated interest in Namibia's PEL104 exploration licence, expanding its holdings in the country. The company aims to be the first to produce oil from Namibia by the end of the decade and plans further exploration efforts.

title: TotalEnergies to power Airbus factories in Germany and the UK with renewables
text: TotalEnergies and Airbus have signed two clean firm power contracts to supply 3.3 TWh of renewable electricity to Airbus's major sites in Germany and the United Kingdom. This supply, starting in 2027 from new renewable assets with a capacity of 200 MW, will cover half of the electricity needs for these sites. The agreement highlights TotalEnergies' ability to provide multi-geography turnkey power solutions and Airbus's commitment to decarbonizing its operations.

title: TotalEnergies inks 3.3 TWh of green power deals with Airbus
text: TotalEnergies has signed agreements with Airbus for the supply of 3.3 TWh of green electricity. These corporate Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) will cover Airbus's European operations in France, Germany, and the UK. The deals aim to support Airbus in its energy transition goals by providing renewable power.

title: TotalEnergies signs 3.3TWh power contract with Airbus for German, British sites
text: TotalEnergies has secured two deals to supply Airbus with 3.3 terawatt-hours of electricity for its German and British sites, covering about half of Airbus's power needs for the next decade. This move aligns with TotalEnergies' strategy to expand its integrated power business in deregulated markets, combining renewable and gas-fired assets to provide continuous power. A portion of the electricity will come from new renewable assets with a capacity of 200 megawatts, with supply expected to begin next year, supporting Airbus's goal for reliable low-carbon energy.

title: Electric mobility: TotalEnergies and Tikehau Capital Join Forces to Develop Public Charging Networks in Belgium and the Netherlands
text: TotalEnergies and Tikehau Capital have formed a joint investment platform to accelerate the development of electric vehicle charging infrastructure in urban public spaces across Belgium and the Netherlands. This partnership will support municipal authorities in their EV transition, aiming to expand existing public concessions and respond to new tenders for urban charging networks. TotalEnergies will provide its expertise in operating charging infrastructure powered by certified renewable energy, while benefiting from Tikehau Capital's capital contribution to strengthen its electric mobility business model.

title: Kuwait: TotalEnergies and Kuwait Oil Company Sign Technical Cooperation Agreement
text: TotalEnergies and Kuwait Oil Company (KOC) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) at the 5th Kuwait Oil & Gas Show and Conference. This agreement aims to foster cooperation, share expertise, and conduct technical studies, particularly focusing on new exploration opportunities in Kuwait. The collaboration underscores a shared ambition to develop Kuwait's natural resources and deepen the long-term relationship between the two entities.

title: TotalEnergies Restarts Mozambique LNG Construction Activities
text: TotalEnergies has announced the restart of construction activities for its Mozambique LNG project, which had been under a force majeure declaration for approximately five years due to security concerns. The restart comes despite a new legal challenge in France accusing the company of "complicity in war crimes" related to alleged civilian killings in 2021, which TotalEnergies denies. The project is expected to deliver its first LNG in 2029, with 40% progress already achieved, and aims to develop 65 trillion cubic feet of gas deposits.

title: TotalEnergies on track to deliver LNG in Mozambique in 2029, CEO says
text: TotalEnergies CEO Patrick Pouyanne announced that the company is on track to deliver LNG from its Mozambique project in 2029, with a massive ramp-up in activity expected soon. This comes as the $20 billion LNG plant is being relaunched after a nearly five-year hiatus due to an Islamist militant attack. TotalEnergies will also provide financial aid to Mozambique following recent deadly floods.

title: TotalEnergies Ends Five-Year Halt on $20 Billion Mozambique LNG
text: TotalEnergies is formally restarting construction on its $20 billion liquefied natural gas project in Mozambique, ending a nearly five-year halt. The resumption will be marked by an event led by President Daniel Chapo and attended by Total CEO Patrick Pouyanne. This project represents one of Africa's largest-ever investments.

title: Why I Keep Buying More Shares of This Amazing High-Yield Dividend Stock for 2026
text: The author continues to invest in TotalEnergies (NYSE: TTE) due to its high dividend yield of 5.6% and diversified business model, which includes electricity production. title: LNG buyers prioritising supply security over price, TotalEnergies executive says
text: An executive from TotalEnergies stated that global instability is causing LNG buyers to prioritize supply security over pricing. Buyers are opting for contracts with companies like TotalEnergies that have diverse LNG portfolios, allowing cargo redirection to mitigate disruptions from crises such as the Ukraine invasion, COVID-19, or the Panama drought. This approach ensures consistent energy delivery despite geopolitical and logistical challenges.

title: Libya Extends Waha Concessions to 2050
text: Libya, along with ConocoPhillips and TotalEnergies SE, has extended the onshore Waha concessions until December 2050. This agreement introduces new fiscal terms aimed at increasing production from the concessions, which currently yield around 370,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, and paves the way for new investments including the development of the North Gialo field. The extension aligns with TotalEnergies' strategy for growth and production from low-cost, low-emission resources.

title: TotalEnergies CEO predicts EU SAF mandate to be dropped in future
text: Patrick Pouyanné, CEO of TotalEnergies, expects the EU's sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) mandate to be revised or dropped due to high costs, supply limitations, and competitive disadvantages for European airlines. He believes market-based incentives are more effective than fixed quotas for driving SAF adoption. These comments underscore the ongoing industry debate about balancing climate goals with commercial viability and energy security.

title: TotalEnergies to supply 800 GWh of renewable power to SWM in France
text: TotalEnergies has secured a contract to supply 800 GWh of renewable electricity annually to SWM, a French professional services company. This partnership aims to provide SWM with green power for 15 years, supporting its sustainability goals. The renewable energy will be sourced from TotalEnergies' portfolio of solar and wind farms in France.

title: France: TotalEnergies to Supply 800 GWh of Renewable Electricity to Paper Manufacturer SWM Over 10 Years
text: TotalEnergies has signed a 10-year contract to supply 800 GWh of renewable electricity to SWM's three paper manufacturing plants in France, starting January 2026. This agreement will provide SWM with a competitive, stable, and low-carbon electricity supply, supporting its decarbonization efforts and aiming to significantly reduce its Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 2033. The electricity will come from approximately 50 MW of TotalEnergies' existing renewable generation assets in France.

title: TotalEnergies stock rating downgraded to Reduce by Kepler Cheuvreux
text: Kepler Cheuvreux has downgraded TotalEnergies SE (EPA:TTE) (NYSE:TTE) from Hold to Reduce, setting a new price target of EUR52.00. This downgrade is driven by the firm's anticipation of an oil price glut and concerns over declining LNG and TTF gas prices, projecting them to fall as low as USD5/mbtu by 2028. TotalEnergies and Equinor are identified as having the highest exposure to a severe LNG glut despite current geopolitical tensions.

title: TotalEnergies signs 10-year green power deal with papermaker SWM
text: TotalEnergies has signed a 10-year agreement to supply 800 gigawatt-hours of renewable electricity to papermaker SWM at three sites in France. This deal, which commenced this month, is part of TotalEnergies' strategy to expand its integrated power business and helps SWM secure half of its French electricity needs from renewable sources for the next decade, significantly reducing its Scope 1 and 2 emissions. TotalEnergies aims to increase its electricity production by approximately 20% annually, reaching 100 terawatt-hours by 2030, through similar agreements with other major companies.

The innovation aims to improve the patient experience for those undergoing frequent treatments for multiple myeloma.

title: Sanofi: FDA Approves Sarclisa Escena, First Cancer Drug via Portable Injector
text: The FDA has approved Sanofi's Sarclisa Escena, a subcutaneous formulation of Sarclisa, for the treatment of multiple myeloma. This marks the first cancer treatment to be administered via a portable on-body injector (Enable Injections' CirCLIQ), offering both this method and manual injection. The approval is supported by the IRAKLIA trial, which confirmed the non-inferiority and a favorable safety profile of the subcutaneous administration compared to intravenous infusion.

title: Commission seeks feedback on commitments offered by Sanofi over possible anticompetitive conduct regarding the promotion of a flu vaccine for vulnerable patients

title: EU seeks feedback on Sanofi’s commitments addressing suspected anti-competitive behaviour

title: Sanofi to stop disparaging rival flu vaccine to stave off EU antitrust fine
text: French pharmaceutical company Sanofi has offered to publicly state that a rival flu vaccine, Fluad by CSL Seqirus, is as effective as its own Efluelda vaccine to avoid a potential EU antitrust fine. The EU initiated an investigation into Sanofi for allegedly disparaging Fluad, primarily in France and Germany, which could have restricted competition. Sanofi's proposal includes publishing corrective statements on its French and German websites for two years and refraining from negatively portraying Fluad, implying superior safety or effectiveness of Efluelda, or mischaracterizing scientific studies, with the offer valid until March 2030 if accepted by the EU competition watchdog.

This data supports Cenrifki's mechanism of targeting chronic inflammation and provides evidence that New Gd+ T1 and new/enlarging T2 lesions may not be standalone markers for treatment modification, especially following its EU approval for non-relapsing secondary progressive MS.

title: EAN 2026: Sanofi’s Cenrifki post hoc data suggests lesions may not indicate failure

Microsoft announces appointment of Carmine Di Sibio to board of directors

REDMOND, Wash. — May 14, 2026 — Microsoft Corp. on Thursday announced the appointment of Carmine Di Sibio, former global
chairman and CEO of EY, to the Microsoft board of directors. He will serve on both the Compensation Committee and Audit Committee, bringing
expertise in financial services, risk oversight and global client leadership to meet the evolving needs of
our customers while advancing Microsoft’s mission to empower every person and organization to achieve more. With Di Sibio’s appointment, the
Microsoft board of directors has been expanded to 13 members.

“Our board will immediately benefit from Carmine’s deep financial expertise, global lens and decades of advising organizations
through real complexity,” said Sandra Peterson, Microsoft lead independent director. “His addition strengthens the board, and we look forward
to working with him.”

“Carmine has spent four decades advising some of the world’s most complex organizations on strategy, financial risk and global
growth,” said Satya Nadella, chairman and CEO, Microsoft. “That depth of experience will strengthen our board as we work to deliver on our
mission and meet the evolving needs of our customers.”

Di Sibio joined EY in 1985, leading to a four-decade career at the company. Before becoming the CEO and global chairman of EY, Di Sibio held
various leadership positions including the global managing partner in Client Services, leading the execution of the organization’s global
strategy, as well as the chair of the Global Financial Services Markets and the regional managing partner
for the Americas Financial Services Organization (FSO). He brings decades of global leadership experience advising leading companies on
strategy and risk management.

Di Sibio holds a Bachelor of Arts in chemistry from Colgate University and an MBA from New
York University’s Stern School of Business. He is also an independent director on the boards of PayPal Holdings, Inc., Prudential Financial,
Inc. and Evolver, in addition to board member positions at Hackensack Meridien Hospital, Colgate
University and Wake Forest University Business School.
